title: The digital yuan is only part of China’s expanding global payments network
gist: China is building multiple overlapping payment layers — a re-engineered interest-bearing e-CNY, the wholesale mBridge, the new bilateral CBETS platform, and a fast-growing CIPS (182.8T RMB Jan–Oct 2026, already above all of 2025) — so renminbi reach can grow even if any single platform stalls. The Iran war/Hormuz renminbi settlement drove a CIPS surge with volumes still 50% above pre-March levels; the author sees no near-term dollar displacement but long-run reshaping of payment rails.

themes.theme: Domestic e-CNY redesign: from digital cash to deposit money

insights.claim: Since January 1, 2026 the PBOC requires commercial banks to pay interest on verified e-CNY wallet balances at demand-deposit rates (~0.05%), letting banks book wallets as deposit liabilities and giving them incentive to push adoption.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Shifts e-CNY economics to banks; watch whether balances grow as the adoption test.
insights.quote: they can now treat e-CNY held in wallets as a deposit liability that they manage on their own balance sheets

insights.claim: The PBOC tripled the number of e-CNY operating banks to thirty, including city commercial banks for the first time.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Broader distribution network for the digital yuan.

insights.claim: Retail e-CNY adoption remains weak despite nearly 230 million personal wallets, partly due to competition from Alipay and WeChat Pay.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Private payment incumbents retain dominance in Chinese retail; e-CNY is not displacing them.
insights.locator: Adoption for the retail e-CNY has been weak.

insights.claim: All-time e-CNY transactions reached about 31 trillion renminbi (~$4.6 trillion) by end-September 2026, double the figure ten months earlier; September value rose 123% YoY while transaction count rose only 12%, likely reflecting large-business and public-sector payments rather than retail.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: e-CNY growth is wholesale/institutional, not consumer — temper retail CBDC adoption narratives.
insights.quote: in September, transaction value rose 123 percent year on year, while the number of transactions rose just 12 percent
insights.locator: Adoption for the retail e-CNY has been weak.

insights.claim: Retail e-CNY balances now sit on commercial bank balance sheets, earn interest and carry deposit insurance, making them look like 'digital deposit money' rather than a central bank liability, even though a March draft finance law still treats e-CNY as digital cash.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Blurs CBDC classification; relevant for comparative CBDC/stablecoin regulatory design.
insights.locator: The debate about whether the digital yuan

insights.claim: In October the PBOC unveiled DCEPS, consolidating e-CNY issuance, retail and wholesale payments and smart contracts onto one platform; the PBOC steps back from holding retail balances but retains control of the rails.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: State control over payment rails persists even as balances are bank-held.
insights.quote: the PBOC is stepping back from holding retail balances but will still maintain control of the rails they run on

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's central bank left Project mBridge after completing its proof of concept in May 2025, a departure reported over a year later, which could hurt mBridge's commodity-trade ambitions.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Weakens the oil-settlement-in-CBDC narrative for mBridge.
insights.locator: The central banks behind Project mBridge

insights.claim: Macau and Mongolia joined mBridge in June 2026; on day one three Macau banks completed twenty-three transactions worth nearly $161 million with mainland China, Hong Kong and the UAE.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: mBridge membership is growing in China's orbit rather than among major commodity exporters.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, mBridge added two members in June

insights.claim: CBETS, a PBOC cross-border e-CNY platform largely ignored by Washington, signed twenty-six first direct participants including Standard Chartered China on June 16, 2026, covering eight jurisdictions from Hong Kong to Brazil.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: An under-the-radar renminbi settlement channel; Western banks are participating.
insights.quote: That PBOC cross-border project Lu mentioned is one that Washington has largely ignored.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, mBridge added two members in June

insights.claim: CBETS connects China's e-CNY system bilaterally to each partner's payment system and settles 24/7; examples include a Xiamen importer paying for Malaysian durian in thirty minutes and China Southern Power Grid cutting Laos electricity settlement from three working days to under five hours.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Real trade-settlement use cases demonstrate speed advantage over correspondent banking.

insights.claim: A bilateral CBETS link may be politically easier for some countries than joining multilateral mBridge, which has become a geopolitical issue, though international demand for e-CNY remains unclear.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Bilateral rails lower the political cost for countries hedging against US financial oversight.

insights.claim: PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng claimed the renminbi's share of international payments rises from 3–4% (fifth, per SWIFT) to 6–7% (third) once CIPS and banks' internal systems are included.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: SWIFT data may understate RMB internationalization; track alternative measures.
insights.locator: China’s most important project perhaps remains CIPS.

insights.claim: CIPS processed 7.7 million transactions worth 182.8 trillion renminbi (~$27 trillion) from January to October 2026, already exceeding its full-year 2025 total; October alone was 807,000 transactions worth 20.5 trillion renminbi.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Rapid CIPS growth is a measurable de-dollarization indicator.
insights.quote: it processed 7.7 million transactions worth 182.8 trillion renminbi (roughly $27 trillion), already surpassing its total for all of 2025
insights.locator: CIPS is a renminbi messaging and settlement

insights.claim: As of end-September 2026 CIPS had 214 direct and 1,651 indirect participants across 133 countries and regions; in September eleven foreign banks joined as direct participants (first direct access for Rwanda, Turkey, Uzbekistan) and Ecobank, across thirty-four African markets, agreed to join in October.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Direct participation bypasses SWIFT messaging, reducing US visibility into RMB transactions — a sanctions-enforcement concern.
insights.locator: Over the past two years, the operator of CIPS

insights.claim: In July CIPS Co. signed a memorandum of cooperation with Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing, broadening CIPS from trade payments toward cross-border stock and bond settlement.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Positive for HKEX as RMB capital-markets settlement hub.
insights.locator: Over the past two years, the operator of CIPS

themes.theme: Iran war as a CIPS stress test

insights.claim: After the Iran war began in late February 2026, Tehran controlled Strait of Hormuz traffic and reportedly charged some vessel fees in renminbi, while China, buying over 80% of Iran's seaborne oil, increasingly settled in renminbi to limit US oversight.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Geopolitical shocks accelerate RMB oil settlement — a structural headwind for dollar dominance in sanctioned trade.

insights.claim: CIPS volumes surged in March 2026 and remain 50 percent above pre-March levels, which alongside new bank onboarding suggests a sustained long-term shift rather than only capital-flight-driven spike.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Persistent post-shock usage implies sticky adoption of alternative rails.
insights.quote: settlement volumes remain 50 percent above pre-March levels

insights.claim: China's multilayer strategy does not depend on any single platform succeeding; the networks are unlikely to displace dollar payment rails soon but will reshape trade-payment infrastructure over time.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: De-dollarization is gradual infrastructure build, not a sudden shift — position for slow erosion, not collapse.
insights.quote: These efforts are unlikely to displace the dollar-based payment networks anytime soon
insights.locator: China’s approach does not depend on a single platform

insights.claim: Signposts for 2027: whether interest-bearing e-CNY lifts holdings, whether mBridge becomes a Hong Kong commercial entity and who joins, whether CBETS publishes transaction data, and whether CIPS volumes keep pace with membership.
insights.speaker: achhangani
insights.so_what: Concrete watchlist for tracking Chinese payment-rail progress.
